Key Contribution: Comprehensive survey of TinyML methods (compression, efficient architectures, deployment stacks) and evaluation practices, providing an updated taxonomy and research map
Limitations / Open Challenges: Limited treatment of embodied robotics constraints (real-time control loops, runtime verification) and distributed multi-robot updates under communication constraints.

Key Contribution: Recent survey consolidating pruning, quantization, distillation, and architecture-level efficiency, with emphasis on deploying DNNs on constrained devices
Limitations / Open Challenges: Robotics-specific closed-loop requirements (stability, safety margins, schedulability) and field-deployment evaluation remain underrepresented.

Key Contribution: Proposes memory-efficient Transformer inference for longer-context workloads on constrained devices, targeting practical edge execution
Limitations / Open Challenges: Robotics embodiment effects (sensor noise, contact dynamics) and system-level integration (perception--planning--control under deadlines) are not the primary validation focus.

Key Contribution: Survey of techniques for optimizing Transformer inference, covering algorithmic and systems-level methods (memory efficiency, kernel/serving optimizations, quantization, and sparsity)
Limitations / Open Challenges: Survey-level: does not establish embodied robotics benchmarks; robustness, real-time guarantees, and safety under closed-loop interaction remain open.

Key Contribution: Provides a recent review of optimization-based MRTA strategies, including taxonomies, trends, and open research directions relevant to dynamic environments
Limitations / Open Challenges: Survey emphasizes optimization methods; explicit coupling to modern edge/IoT constraints (distributed compute, on-device learning, semantic reasoning) remains an open systems challenge.

Key Contribution: Experimental evaluation of edge/fog robotics readiness, highlighting practical benefits and bottlenecks of current network/virtualization technologies for robotics workloads
Limitations / Open Challenges: Findings are application- and stack-dependent; general benchmarks for heterogeneous robots, safety constraints, and harsh-field conditions remain incomplete.
